issue: closeNode guards only pruned-to-live moves and keeps 'active' in CLOSE_STATUSES, so a node closed as exhausted, answered, blocked or abstained can be revived as active, despite its docstring promise to 'move a node to a later lifecycle status'. A shipped caller sends this: in deep-review.yaml, active_frontier_node is bound once at line 1184; the stuck-recovery branch (lines 1599-1605) closes it as exhausted and re-runs the reducer but never rebinds it, and step_frontier_activate (lines 1699-1704) then closes the same id as active. The stuck node is revived, counts toward frontierOpen (vetoing the stop), and is redispatched, so stuck recovery cannot retire it and the run can cycle until maxIterations. Fix: refuse moves from a terminal status (answered, blocked, exhausted, abstained) back to active, with a test for that case, and/or rebind active_frontier_node after the stuck close.

issue: On an expansive research run, a frontier node closed as exhausted with reason budget makes its question resolved (line 2684). The write-back then marks it '- [x]' in the strategy key questions, lists it under ANSWERED QUESTIONS and saves it as resolved in the registry. On the next reduce, question.checked is true, so line 2664 puts the node in answeredNodeIds, and applyFrontierBudget and buildFrontierProjection flip it from 'exhausted' to 'answered'. From then on the frontier stats, the dashboard FRONTIER section and frontierStatus report unanswered, budget-closed work as answered, and a later run_extended that raises maxIterations can never reopen the node. Reach: every expansive run whose band spend reaches its share, because the workflow's reduce writes the strategy each iteration. No test reduces twice, so nothing catches it. Fix: build answeredNodeIds only from evidence (resolutionRecords, or a checked question that frontierClose did not resolve), and keep a frontier-closed question out of ANSWERED QUESTIONS and out of the persisted checked flag, or persist frontierStatus and let it win over checked.
